parts.name: green body shell

physics.Basic_description: Dark green painted metal forming the base, fuel tank, and top cap assembly with a smooth, semi-gloss finish.
physics.Functional_description: Structural housing that contains the fuel reservoir and supports the glass globe and burner mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the cylindrical base or the top cap firmly with parallel jaws to lift or stabilize the lantern.
physics.reason: Standard sheet metal construction for lantern bodies implies a thin shell enclosing air or fuel, not a solid block.

parts.description: Dark green painted metal forming the base, fuel tank, and top cap assembly with a smooth, semi-gloss finish.
parts.function: Structural housing that contains the fuel reservoir and supports the glass globe and burner mechanism.

parts.name: globe glass

physics.Basic_description: Translucent white frosted glass bulb situated centrally between the metal frame arms.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the flame from wind while diffusing light outward.
physics.Grasped_description: Avoid grasping directly due to fragility and slipperiness; if necessary, use soft compliant fingertips with minimal force.
physics.reason: Glass globes are blown or molded shells with significant wall thickness for heat resistance but are hollow inside.

parts.description: Translucent white frosted glass bulb situated centrally between the metal frame arms.
parts.function: Protects the flame from wind while diffusing light outward.

parts.name: draft tube 0

physics.Basic_description: Two vertical dark green metal tubes curving along the sides of the glass globe.
physics.Functional_description: Channels air from the base to the top to create a draft for efficient combustion and structural support.
physics.Grasped_description: Ideal grasp point for lifting; grip one or both tubes vertically with parallel jaws.
physics.reason: Draft tubes are thin-walled conduits for air flow, not solid rods.

parts.name: burner wick

physics.Basic_description: Small yellowish fibrous tip protruding from the center of the burner assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Draws fuel up via capillary action to sustain the flame.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and fragile to grasp; manipulation would damage the wick.
physics.reason: A wick is a dense bundle of fibers, effectively solid for manipulation purposes.

parts.name: flame

physics.Basic_description: Small orange glowing region representing the fire at the wick tip.
physics.Functional_description: Source of light and heat generated by combustion.
physics.Grasped_description: Intangible and hazardous; cannot be grasped.
physics.reason: Flame is a volume of gas/plasma, treated as solid volume for segmentation but has no physical wall.

parts.description: Small orange glowing region representing the fire at the wick tip.

parts.name: vent slot 0

physics.Basic_description: Series of small dark purple rectangular openings or slats around the upper chimney section.
physics.Functional_description: Allows hot gases and smoke to escape from the top of the lantern.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to grasp individually; part of the larger top assembly.
physics.reason: These are openings in the thin metal sheet of the chimney.

parts.name: apex seat

physics.Basic_description: Small cyan-colored ring or collar at the very top of the chimney where the handle attaches.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a mounting point and pivot for the carrying handle.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp securely on its own; usually grasped as part of the top assembly.
physics.reason: Likely a stamped or cast metal ring with a central hole, effectively a thin-walled structure.

parts.description: Small cyan-colored ring or collar at the very top of the chimney where the handle attaches.
parts.function: Provides a mounting point and pivot for the carrying handle.

parts.name: top eye stem

physics.Basic_description: Small magenta-colored vertical pin or stem connecting the top ring to the apex.
physics.Functional_description: Structural link holding the carrying ring in place.
physics.Grasped_description: Too thin to grasp reliably without slipping.
physics.reason: Small pins and stems are typically solid metal wire or rod for strength.

parts.description: Small magenta-colored vertical pin or stem connecting the top ring to the apex.

parts.name: top eye ring

physics.Basic_description: Small pink-colored metal loop at the very top of the lantern assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Attachment point for hanging the lantern or securing the handle.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be hooked or pinched with fine gripper tips, though the main handle is preferred.
physics.reason: Small rings are typically formed from solid wire stock.

parts.description: Small pink-colored metal loop at the very top of the lantern assembly.
parts.function: Attachment point for hanging the lantern or securing the handle.

parts.name: hanger ring wire

physics.Basic_description: Large lime-green/yellow wire loop arching over the top of the lantern.
physics.Functional_description: Primary handle for carrying the lantern by hand or hanging it from a hook.
physics.Grasped_description: Excellent grasp target; pinch the top arc of the wire with parallel jaws to lift the entire object.
physics.reason: Handle wires are solid metal rods bent into shape, not hollow tubes.

parts.description: Large lime-green/yellow wire loop arching over the top of the lantern.

parts.name: knob knurled disk

physics.Basic_description: Small teal-colored textured disk located on the side of the fuel tank base.
physics.Functional_description: User interface for adjusting the wick height and flame intensity.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch the edges of the disk with fingertips to rotate and adjust the wick.
physics.reason: Knobs are typically solid cast or machined metal pieces for durability and grip.

parts.description: Small teal-colored textured disk located on the side of the fuel tank base.

physics.Functional_description: Visual indicator or tactile aid for rotating the wick knob.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp independently; manipulated indirectly via the main knob.
physics.reason: Integral part of the solid knob assembly.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
